meta.project: Bilingual, Ontology-Aware, and Explainable ESG Intelligence System
meta.description: Consolidated reference mapping linking integrated research objectives (v-1 to v3) with causal traceability to curated literature evidence.

research_questions: RQ1.1: How can Transformer-based architectures be optimized for bilingual ESG ABSA?
RQ1.3: How can regional calibration and ESG lexicons mitigate bias?

literature_references.title: Improving Zero-shot Cross-lingual Transfer between Closely Related Languages by injecting Character-level Noise
literature_references.relevance: Provides causal evidence for C3 and RQ1.1 by demonstrating that character-level noise improves zero-shot transfer for related language varieties, essential for Indonesian-English ESG coverage.

literature_references.title: Morphosyntactic Tagging with Pre-trained Language Models for Arabic and its Dialects
literature_references.authors: Go Inoue, Salam Khalifa, Nizar Habash
literature_references.relevance: Supports RQ1.3 and C1 by validating that strategic fine-tuning with high-resource data from other dialects is beneficial for low-resource regional calibration.

contributions: C8: Large-scale ESG LLM benchmark (30+ models)
research_questions: RQ2.1: To what extent does few-shot learning improve ESG granularity?
RQ2.4: How can multi-LLM fusion reduce hallucination?
RQ2.2: How can long-context mechanisms enhance scalability?

literature_references.title: DS2-ABSA: Dual-Stream Data Synthesis with Label Refinement for Few-Shot Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis
literature_references.authors: Hongling Xu, Yice Zhang, Qianlong Wang, Ruifeng Xu
literature_references.relevance: Directly supports C16 and RQ2.1 by introducing a dual-stream synthesis framework to address data scarcity and improve granularity in low-resource ABSA.

literature_references.title: MoEfication: Transformer Feed-forward Layers are Mixtures of Experts
literature_references.authors: Zhengyan Zhang, Yankai Lin, Zhiyuan Liu, Peng Li, Maosong Sun, Jie Zhou
literature_references.relevance: Provides architectural justification for C10 and RQ2.4, showing how expert routers within models can conditionally activate partitions to improve efficiency and robustness.

research_questions: RQ3.1: How can symbolic reasoning be integrated using ESG ontologies?
RQ3.2: How can transparent outputs be ensured via reasoning graphs?
RQ3.3: How can implicit ESG claims be identified?

literature_references.title: Fact-Tree Reasoning for N-ary Question Answering over Knowledge Graphs
literature_references.authors: Yao Zhang, Peiyao Li, Hongru Liang, Adam Jatowt, Zhenglu Yang
literature_references.relevance: Establishes the logic for C7 and RQ3.2, showing that upgrading from linear chains to tree-structured fact reasoning improves interpretability in complex graph scenarios.

literature_references.title: XPrompt: Explaining Large Language Model's Generation via Joint Prompt Attribution
literature_references.authors: Yurui Chang, Bochuan Cao, Yujia Wang, Jinghui Chen, Lu Lin
literature_references.relevance: Supports C15 and RQ3.2 by providing a counterfactual framework to explain how combined prompt inputs collaboratively influence model generation.

research_questions: RQ4.1: How can XAI improve stakeholder trust in ESG outputs?
RQ4.5: Can tone–outcome mismatch reliably indicate greenwashing?

literature_references.title: Error Comparison Optimization for Large Language Models on Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis
literature_references.authors: Qianlong Wang, Keyang Ding, H. Gao, H. Wang, Ruifeng Xu
literature_references.relevance: Crucial for C11 and RQ4.5; introduces a framework to perceive error degrees in ABSA, which is vital for distinguishing between mild sentiment shifts and severe greenwashing risk.

literature_references.title: Factual Consistency of Multilingual Pretrained Language Models
literature_references.relevance: Provides a baseline for RQ4.1, demonstrating the high degree of factual inconsistency in multilingual models and justifying the need for trust metrics.

research_questions: RQ5.1: How can transparent and auditable outputs be ensured?
RQ5.2: How can reasoning quality and consistency be operationalized at scale?

literature_references.title: Attention Mechanism with Energy-Friendly Operations
literature_references.authors: Yu Wan, Baosong Yang, Dayiheng Liu, Rong Xiao, Derek F. Wong, Haibo Zhang, Boxing Chen, Lidia S. Chao
literature_references.relevance: Enables the scalability and operational efficiency goals of C12 and RQ5.2 by reducing energy/compute costs during the attention procedure.

literature_references.title: Enhancing Open-Domain Task-Solving Capability of LLMs via Autonomous Tool Integration from GitHub
literature_references.relevance: Supports the system extensibility of C12 and O5 by providing a framework for autonomous integration of specialized tools into LLM-based agent systems.
